status: 4d78a GPIO5 digital RX retest failed before protocol decoding

measurements.mainHardwareDifference: new MOSFET-only TX driver without previous 2N3904 stage
measurements.currentRxFrontEnd: TEPT4400 into LM393 comparator; TEPT4400 on +IN, 10k potentiometer threshold from 3.3V on -IN

interpretation: GPIO5 digital RX is not seeing valid HIGH logic from the current phototransistor node.
RX decodes mostly invalid bytes and never detects a valid 0xAA preamble run.
Failure is before CRC/FEC/file reconstruction.
Low-frequency tests at 1 Hz and 30 Hz show TX can fully turn ON/OFF and RX can swing about 0.1 V to 3 V.
The likely bottleneck is frequency response, RC settling, sampling phase, or high-rate optical contrast collapse.
An earlier matched RX/TX setup transmitted text at about 9 kHz, so current 9 kHz failure should be treated as a regression or setup mismatch rather than a hard project limit.
The only reported hardware difference is the new MOSFET-only TX driver without 2N3904, so TX driver waveform behavior at 9 kHz is a leading suspect.
Latest RX log is mostly 0xFF and 0x55, with no RX_FRAME_START, no carousel frames, and digital captures reporting high=0/transitions=0.
The 1 Hz digital capture used only 100 ms, shorter than the 500 ms half-bit, so slow tests need RXCAP=2000,100.
Repeated 0x55 during slow tests suggests alternating waveform with polarity/phase mismatch.
Older working protocol may have been the packet CRC era, not carousel. Closest repo match is firmware/experiments/packet_tx and packet_rx from around commit 1071b27.
Created branch experiment/packet-crc-active-high-mosfet with active-high packet CRC TX/RX sketches in firmware/experiments/packet_crc_active_high_tx and packet_crc_active_high_rx.
Added packet CRC GUI apps/experiments/packet_crc_gui.py and launcher scripts/run_packet_crc_gui.sh. Stable carousel GUI should not be used for this packet test.
Packet CRC GUI now has shared, RX-only, and TX-only terminals plus timestamped Save buttons. Logs live in debug_logs/packet_crc_gui_shared_*.log, packet_crc_gui_rx_*.log, and packet_crc_gui_tx_*.log.

Latest packet test 20260519_152255: TX sent packets, RX had no RX_PACKET_OK; INV=1 was tried; 9000 Hz capture had high=0/transitions=0, but 200 Hz capture saw high=1218 low=18571 transitions=882. Repeated wrong bytes 0x03 0xFB 0xFF 0xC8 suggest sync edge/phase/polarity timing issue.
Shared ChatGPT conversation https://chatgpt.com/share/69fddf92-1a34-83ec-9f7d-1dd195c277cd was fetched and saved as debug_logs/shared_chatgpt_69fddf92.html.
That shared conversation points more strongly to the carousel/file-transfer era than the packet CRC era: the old problem was missing the final short image chunk, not total RX sync failure.
The old working-style TX hardware in that conversation used a 2N3904 inverter with IRF540N gate pull-up. Firmware was active-low idle-ON: GPIO LOW means LED ON, GPIO HIGH means LED OFF.

Local matching files are .history/firmware/stable/tx/tx_20260509042645.ino, .history/apps/stable/Tx_gui_20260509042013.py, .history/apps/stable/Rx_gui_20260509042004.py, and .history/firmware/stable/rx/rx_20260509041644.ino.
Old shared-session test recipe was 9000 Hz, 512-byte chunks, 3 carousel rounds, with final short chunk padded optically while RX saves only real_len bytes.
Because current TX no longer uses 2N3904, software can mimic idle-ON/padded carousel framing, but it cannot fully reproduce the old gate-drive edge speed and optical waveform.
GPIO5 digital mode cannot use a firmware-set 1 V threshold; use GPIO34 ADC or a comparator/Schmitt stage.
A 5 V phototransistor front-end must be level-limited before any ESP32 GPIO/ADC input.
Current RX hardware update: TEPT4400 feeds LM393 comparator, with TEPT4400 on +IN and 10k potentiometer threshold on -IN.
Latest TEPT4400 measurement: light present drives the sensor node near 0 V; no light drives it to about 2.3 V.
LM393 output should be pulled up to 3.3 V when feeding ESP32 GPIO.
With this LM393 polarity, expected comparator output is light ON = LOW and light OFF/dark = HIGH. For current active-high packet TX, packet RX should try INV=1 first.

Latest packet test 20260519_231343: TX sent SEND=1 at 9000 Hz, RX was INV=0, and RX logged many RX_ERROR:unstable_manchester_bit lines with no RX_PACKET_OK. Next test should start at 1000 Hz with INV=1 and RXCAP=2000,50.
